bugs.title: ViT local layer spec uses AttnMaskType.causal instead of no_mask, silently turning bidirectional self-attention into causal
bugs.root_cause: get_vit_layer_with_local_spec set self_attention attn_mask_type to AttnMaskType.causal. ViTs require bidirectional attention over patch tokens, so a lower-triangular mask is applied by DotProductAttention every forward pass. The TE path was already correct (no_mask) by an earlier fix; only the local path was missed. Training proceeds normally, but every patch can only attend to earlier patches, distorting visual features.
bugs.invariant: ViT SelfAttention.attn_mask_type must be AttnMaskType.no_mask in both TE and local layer specs.
trigger_conditions: ViT/CLIP encoder built via get_vit_layer_with_local_spec (non-TE local path)
Multimodal training (LLaVA-style) with image patch tokens

bugs.title: GPTDataset returns aliased cached_loss_mask, downstream in-place padding mutates the shared cache and corrupts later samples
bugs.root_cause: In the cached-mask branch, GPTDataset assigned loss_mask = self.cached_loss_mask, returning the cached tensor by reference instead of a clone. Downstream code in the same __getitem__ path applies in-place modifications (e.g. zeroing the loss for pad tokens). The first sample with padding silently mutates the shared cache, so every subsequent sample served from the cache starts from a polluted mask.
bugs.invariant: GPTDataset.cached_loss_mask must equal a tensor of all-ones at the start of every __getitem__ call.
trigger_conditions: create_attention_mask=False so the cached-mask branch is taken
Sequences with padding so loss_mask is mutated per-sample by mask_loss_or_position fill

bugs.title: Megatron-FSDP GradReducePipeline scales gbuf.data instead of bucket.data, applying gradient scaling to the wrong tensor span
bugs.root_cause: GradReducePipeline.gradient_reduce_preprocessing was passed gbuf.data (the entire buffer) instead of bucket.data (the per-bucket slice). gradient_scaling preprocessing therefore divided every byte of the joint gradient buffer once per bucket, yielding cumulative scaling factor of (1/dp_size)**num_buckets on the affected ranges instead of (1/dp_size). All-reduce/reduce-scatter then communicated wrongly scaled gradients with no shape mismatch.
bugs.invariant: After gradient_reduce_preprocessing, the magnitude of bucket.data must equal the pre-scaled magnitude divided by gradient_scaling_factor (not by gradient_scaling_factor**num_buckets).

bugs.title: DistributedDataParallel target_gradient_scaling_factor uses get_data_parallel_world_size without context_parallel, so gradients are over-scaled by cp_size when CP is enabled
bugs.root_cause: DistributedDataParallel computed target_gradient_scaling_factor = 1.0 / parallel_state.get_data_parallel_world_size() without with_context_parallel=True. With CP enabled the gradient reduction collective spans the dp*cp ranks, so the gradients should be divided by dp_size*cp_size. Only dividing by dp_size leaves a residual factor of cp_size in the parameter updates.
bugs.invariant: When context_parallel_size > 1, the gradient_scaling_factor used by DDP must be 1 / (data_parallel_world_size * context_parallel_size).

bugs.title: DSA indexer loss is not divided by num_microbatches in forward_step_calc_loss, so the auxiliary loss gradient is overweighted by a factor of num_microbatches
bugs.root_cause: forward_step_calc_loss set MTPLossAutoScaler.set_loss_scale(loss_scale / num_microbatches) but DSAIndexerLossAutoScaler was never given a per-microbatch divisor. As a result the DSA indexer auxiliary loss accumulates num_microbatches times into the gradient instead of being averaged, contributing a (num_microbatches)x larger gradient than the main loss.
bugs.invariant: DSAIndexerLossAutoScaler.loss_scale at backward time must equal loss_scale / num_microbatches when calculate_per_token_loss=False.

bugs.title: TEGroupedMLP fused-ops backward_dw skips _trigger_wgrad_accumulation_and_reduce_hooks on the original linear modules, so DDP never zeros param.grad and AccumulateGrad double-counts
bugs.root_cause: _make_fused_ops creates new GroupedLinear instances for the fused FC1/activation/FC2 path. backward_dw was called on the new instances, but DDP had registered the wgrad-accumulate-and-reduce hooks on the ORIGINAL self.linear_fc1/fc2 modules. Hooks therefore never fired, param.grad was not cleared, and AccumulateGrad performed an additional in-place add into main_grad on the next iteration, silently double-counting expert weight gradients.
bugs.invariant: After every TEGroupedMLP.backward_dw call, _trigger_wgrad_accumulation_and_reduce_hooks must be invoked exactly once on linear_fc1 and once on linear_fc2.
trigger_conditions: TE GroupedLinear with fused operations (TEGroupedMLP fused path)

bugs.title: Interleaved 1F1B forgets to wait on async P2P send before deallocating the source buffer, sending corrupted activations to the next pipeline stage
bugs.root_cause: forward_backward_pipelining_with_interleaving issued an isend to the next stage and immediately called deallocate_output_tensor without waiting on send_next_wait_handle. Because isend's HtoD copy is asynchronous, the destination buffer on the next rank could end up with whatever value happened to be left in memory by the time the deallocation reuse cycle began. Training continued with subtly corrupted forward activations propagated down the pipeline.
bugs.invariant: Whenever deallocate_pipeline_outputs=True, every send_next isend handle must have wait() called before deallocate_output_tensor on the same output_tensor.

bugs.title: prepare_input_tensors_for_wgrad_compute does not enforce all_gathered_input.contiguous(), so wgrad GEMM reads a non-contiguous strided tensor as if it were contiguous
bugs.root_cause: prepare_input_tensors_for_wgrad_compute only called grad_output.contiguous() and assumed all_gathered_input was already contiguous. Some upstream paths (NeMo SFT QAT inputs, some reshape/transpose chains) hand in a strided tensor, but fused_weight_gradient_mlp_cuda.wgrad_gemm_accum_* indexes the buffer via flat data_ptr arithmetic. The kernel reads the wrong elements yet the tensor metadata looks valid, so the wgrad accumulation produces silently incorrect numbers.
bugs.invariant: all_gathered_input.is_contiguous() must be True at the entry of prepare_input_tensors_for_wgrad_compute.
trigger_conditions: Sequence parallel + TP > 1 with non-contiguous gathered activations (e.g. NeMo SFT QAT codepath)

bugs.title: MoE aux loss not scaled by num_tokens in per_token_loss mode
tensor_parallel.checkpoint runs CheckpointFunction during CUDA graph warmup, causing graph capture to record stale recomputed activations
bugs.root_cause: tensor_parallel.checkpoint always dispatched to CheckpointFunction.apply, even during graph warmup or capture. CheckpointFunction tries to recompute the saved forward inside the graph context, which corrupts the captured graph because random states and saved tensors get rewritten between warmup and capture passes. The result is a captured graph that on replay produces values that do not match the eager reference.
bugs.invariant: When is_graph_warmup() or is_graph_capturing() is True, tensor_parallel.checkpoint must invoke function(*args) directly without entering CheckpointFunction.apply.
trigger_conditions: CUDA graph capture for the same module (cuda_graph_modules)

bugs.title: _CudagraphReplayNode unconditionally copies user_input into cudagraph_input even when the data pointers already match, overwriting in-place results from preceding ops
bugs.root_cause: When the user_input tensor is the SAME storage as cudagraph_input (data_ptr equality), copy_ amounts to a self-copy that semantically still launches a kernel. In specific reuse patterns the source and destination data pointers were intentionally identical so no copy was needed, but cudagraph_input.copy_(user_input) was always issued and could overwrite a value that another op had just written, especially under certain stream orderings.
bugs.invariant: cudagraph_input.copy_(user_input) must only be issued when user_input.data_ptr() != cudagraph_input.data_ptr().
trigger_conditions: CUDA graphs enabled with input/output buffer reuse across runners
Sequence of layers where the previous layer's output is the next layer's input alias

bugs.title: DDP cast cudagraph manager runs warmup steps and shares mempool across virtual pipeline stages, corrupting captured param-cast outputs across VPP
bugs.root_cause: _ParamAndGradBucketGroup created a CudaGraphManager for copy_params_from_grad_buffer without num_warmup_steps=0, so the cast graph was warmed up before capture. Combined with cuda_graph_use_single_mempool=True and lack of per-VPP stage scoping, multiple VPP stages shared mempool and warmup buffers, so the captured cast graph for one VPP stage could write into another stage's parameter buffer.
bugs.invariant: DDP cast cudagraphs must be created with num_warmup_steps=0 and tagged with the current vp_stage so that VPP stages do not share captured buffer pools.
trigger_conditions: DDP enable_cuda_graph=True with virtual pipeline parallel (interleaved schedule)
Multiple VPP stages on the same device

bugs.title: DistributedOptimizer FP32 shard_model_param uses non-detached view, so the parameter shard participates in autograd and accumulates spurious grad_fn
bugs.root_cause: _build_model_and_main_param_groups built shard_model_param as model_param.view(-1)[range] without .detach(). Unlike the FP16/BF16 branch (which goes through main_param.detach() copies), the FP32 view kept grad_fn alive. As soon as anything autograd-eligible touched the shard, an extra grad chain was created, leading to silently doubled gradient contributions for FP32 parameters and inconsistent state with the FP16/BF16 path.
bugs.invariant: Every shard_model_param entry created in _build_model_and_main_param_groups must satisfy shard_model_param.requires_grad == False and shard_model_param.grad_fn is None.
trigger_conditions: DistributedOptimizer enabled with FP32 master parameters
Mixed precision training where some params remain FP32 (e.g. embeddings, layernorm)

bugs.title: _ParamAndGradBucket builds local param_to_index from naive concatenation, ignoring per-param padding so optimizer reads from misaligned offsets when distributed optimizer pads to data_parallel_world_size
bugs.root_cause: _ParamAndGradBucket initialized param_to_index by walking params and assigning offset += param.numel(), but the global param_index_map already had per-param padded offsets. The two layouts diverged whenever a param's size was not a multiple of dp_world_size. param_to_index was then used by the distributed optimizer to slice param_data, so the optimizer wrote/read different slices than where the gradients lived.
bugs.invariant: For every param in bucket, bucket.param_to_index[param] must equal (param_index_map[param][0] - bucket.offset, param_index_map[param][1] - bucket.offset).
trigger_conditions: Bucket with multiple params where at least one param.numel() is not a multiple of data_parallel_world_size
Adjacent params therefore receive runtime padding between them

bugs.title: Latent MoE backward_dw never calls fc1_latent_proj/fc2_latent_proj.backward_dw, so gradient for the latent projection weights is silently zero
bugs.root_cause: MoELayer.backward_dw only invoked self.experts.backward_dw() and (when shared_experts requested) self.shared_experts.backward_dw(). The new latent projection layers fc1_latent_proj/fc2_latent_proj were never asked to compute their weight gradients, so their main_grad stayed at zero across every microbatch. The optimizer happily applied (lr * 0) to those parameters every step, freezing them at their initialization.
bugs.invariant: When config.moe_latent_size is set, fc1_latent_proj.backward_dw and fc2_latent_proj.backward_dw must each be called once per backward pass through the MoE layer.
trigger_conditions: MoE layer with config.moe_latent_size set (latent MoE / DeepSeek-style projection)
Fine-grained backward_dw scheduling (separate routed_experts and shared_experts paths)

bugs.title: _CudagraphReplayNode treats fp4_enabled as fp8 only, skipping the per-module FP-recipe restoration on FP4 paths so saved scaling factors drift each replay
bugs.root_cause: _CudagraphReplayNode.forward only checked runner.fp8_enabled when deciding whether to set is_first_microbatch and restore the per-module DelayedScaling recipe. With FP4 active but FP8 inactive, the recipe restore branch was skipped, so each replay used a stale amax history. Every step shifted the FP4 scale away from the target, causing slowly drifting numerics.
bugs.invariant: If runner.fp4_enabled, the per-module DelayedScaling recipe restoration must execute identically to the runner.fp8_enabled path.
trigger_conditions: FP4 (NVFP4) training enabled (config.fp4 set, fp4_recipe DelayedScaling)
CUDA graphs enabled with FP4 modules

bugs.title: _CudaGraphRunner enables FP8 capture for keep-mamba-stack-attention-linear-in-bf16 layers, casting frozen-bf16 attention linears into FP8 inside the captured graph
bugs.root_cause: _CudaGraphRunner.__init__ set self.fp8_enabled = config.fp8 is not None / self.fp4_enabled = config.fp4 is not None unconditionally. The mamba-stack attention linears, however, are kept in bf16 to preserve numerics. Capturing those layers with FP8 enabled wrapped their GEMMs in FP8 cast paths, silently quantizing weights that were intentionally meant to stay in bf16.
bugs.invariant: If isinstance(base_module, TransformerLayer) and config.keep_mamba_stack_attention_linear_in_bf16 and not is_moe_layer, runner.fp8_enabled and runner.fp4_enabled must both be False.
trigger_conditions: CUDA graph capture enabled for transformer layers

bugs.title: TransformerLayer with moe_layer_recompute uses non-FP4-aware te_checkpoint guard, so FP4 recompute uses tensor_parallel.checkpoint and loses FP4 amax tracking
bugs.root_cause: TransformerLayer.forward selected te_checkpoint only when self.config.fp8. With FP4-only training, the gate was False, so the regular tensor_parallel.checkpoint was used. That recompute path does not know about TE's FP recipe machinery: amax history is not extended for the recomputed forward, so the next forward sees an amax that omits the contribution of the recomputed pass, yielding mismatched scales between forward and recompute.
bugs.invariant: When self.is_moe_layer and self.moe_layer_recompute and (config.fp8 or config.fp4), te_checkpoint must be selected as the recompute function.

bugs.title: group_limited_topk uses num_groups instead of topk in inner topk
Attention.set_save_original_input gate is FP8-only and missed for NVFP4, so attention activations are cached as the FP4-quantized tensor instead of the original input
bugs.root_cause: Attention.__init__ guarded set_save_original_input on the linear_proj only when config.fp8 and recipe != delayed. With FP4 training, the guard never fired so linear_proj kept the FP4-quantized tensor cache. When selective recompute later invoked the saved tensor for backward, it operated on the quantized tensor instead of the bf16 original input, producing a recompute that mismatches the forward.
bugs.invariant: set_save_original_input must be called on TELinear modules whenever (config.fp8 with non-delayed recipe and TE>=2.6.0dev0) OR (config.fp4 and TE>=2.7.0.dev0).

bugs.title: MultimodalRotaryEmbedding slices rotary embedding along the wrong dimension and omits cp_group when CP is enabled, so each CP rank sees the wrong rotary position embedding
bugs.root_cause: After emb.transpose(0, 1).contiguous() the sequence dimension is index 0, but get_pos_emb_on_this_cp_rank was called with seq_dim=1 and no cp_group argument. The wrong axis was sharded across CP ranks, and the default global cp_group fallback was used instead of the configured one. Each CP rank ended up with a rotary slice that does not correspond to its own sequence partition.
bugs.invariant: MultimodalRotaryEmbedding output for CP rank r must equal get_pos_emb_on_this_cp_rank(global_emb, seq_dim=0, group=cp_group) for the configured cp_group.
trigger_conditions: MultimodalRotaryEmbedding (mrope) used in a multimodal model
Sequence dimension is dim 0 of the post-transpose tensor

bugs.title: MambaStack assigns make_viewless_tensor result to local 'output' but returns 'hidden_states', sending a non-viewless aliased tensor between hybrid VPP stages
bugs.root_cause: MambaStack.forward stored the result of make_viewless_tensor in a local variable 'output', but the function ultimately returned hidden_states. So the explicit make_viewless_tensor call had no effect. The non-viewless tensor (still a view onto an internal buffer) was returned and forwarded to the next PP stage via isend; on a hybrid VPP schedule the underlying buffer was reused before isend completed, and the next stage received corrupted activations.
bugs.invariant: MambaStack.forward must return a tensor that is viewless (.is_view() == False) so its storage is not aliased with internal stack buffers.
trigger_conditions: Hybrid Mamba model with virtual pipeline parallel (VPP)
Inter-stage tensor sent via PP isend/irecv

bugs.title: Hybrid DSL CommonLayerConfig does not derive params_dtype from mixed_precision_dtype, so models with mixed_precision_dtype='bf16' silently keep params_dtype=fp32
bugs.root_cause: The DSL allowed bf16 mixed-precision compute while keeping params_dtype at fp32, producing a TransformerConfig with bf16=True but params_dtype=torch.float32. The legacy --bf16 CLI path automatically aligns params_dtype with bf16, so the DSL path silently diverged: parameters were materialized in fp32 and then cast on every forward, doubling memory and changing numerics relative to the legacy path.
bugs.invariant: When TransformerConfig.bf16 is True (mixed_precision_dtype='bf16') and the recipe leaves params_dtype at the fp32 default, the produced TransformerConfig.params_dtype must equal torch.bfloat16.
trigger_conditions: Hybrid model built via the new Python DSL recipe API
Recipe sets mixed_precision_dtype='bf16' and leaves params_dtype at its 'fp32' default

bugs.title: ChainedOptimizer.split_state_dict for single-chunk MoE only assigns to state_dicts[0], leaving all other sub-optimizers unaware of the model state and silently skipping their load
bugs.root_cause: split_state_dict's single-model-chunk branch did state_dicts[0] = state_dict only, leaving state_dicts[1:] as None. Sub-optimizers beyond index 0 (e.g. the MoE expert optimizer) thus received None as their model state and silently skipped loading their parameters/optimizer states. The model proceeded with default-initialized expert parameters after a checkpoint resume.
bugs.invariant: After ChainedOptimizer.split_state_dict, every entry in state_dicts must be non-None when state_dict is provided and len(self.model_chunks) == 1.
trigger_conditions: ChainedOptimizer with multiple sub-optimizers (e.g. dense + MoE)

bugs.title: MegatronOptimizer.get_grads_for_norm checks fsdp_param BEFORE precision-aware-optimizer branch, so M-FSDP + precision-aware optimizer reads param.grad._local_tensor instead of decoupled_grad and computes the wrong norm
bugs.root_cause: MegatronOptimizer.get_grads_for_norm gated on getattr(param, '__fsdp_param__', False) FIRST and only fell back to the precision-aware decoupled_grad branch when not an FSDP param. With both flags on, FSDP parameters were always read via param.grad._local_tensor instead of param.decoupled_grad. Under precision-aware optimizer, param.grad is None or stale because gradients are written into param.decoupled_grad. The grad norm computation thus used wrong (likely zero) tensors, silently disabling clipping and giving an incorrect global norm for logging.
bugs.invariant: When config.use_precision_aware_optimizer_no_fp8_or_ds_fp8 is True, get_grads_for_norm must use param.decoupled_grad (with ._local_tensor when also __fsdp_param__) and never use param.grad.
trigger_conditions: Gradient clipping with grad norm computation

bugs.title: Hybrid MoE pad_granularity is set to 32 (MXFP8) instead of 128 (HybridEP), so per-CP-rank sequence shards are misaligned for HybridEP dispatcher
bugs.root_cause: HybridCPDataLoaderWrapper used pad_granularity = 32 (MXFP8 block size) when computing per-rank padding. HybridEP requires alignment to 128 elements. With granularity 32, per-CP-rank shards landed at offsets that did not satisfy HybridEP's 128-element alignment, so the dispatcher's load/store kernels read/wrote across token boundaries, mixing tokens between adjacent ranks.
bugs.invariant: HybridCPDataLoaderWrapper.pad_granularity must equal 128 when HybridEP is enabled (instead of 32).
trigger_conditions: Sequences whose per-rank shard length is not divisible by 128

bugs.title: MegatronOptimizer uses use_precision_aware_optimizer instead of use_precision_aware_optimizer_no_fp8_or_ds_fp8 when selecting decoupled_grad, so FP8 + precision-aware paths read param.decoupled_grad which is None and report grad_norm=0
bugs.root_cause: MegatronOptimizer.get_grads_for_norm and clip_grad_by_total_norm_fp32 dispatched on self.config.use_precision_aware_optimizer. With FP8 enabled, decoupled_grad is intentionally NOT used for those parameters; they should fall back to param.grad. The buggy gate took the precision-aware path anyway, attempting to read param.decoupled_grad (which is None), so grads_for_norm came back empty and grad_norm computed to 0.0. Without proper gradient clipping the optimizer could overshoot, but no exception was raised because count_zeros and clip routines treat empty input as a valid no-op.
bugs.invariant: When config.fp8 is set or config.fp8_recipe in the DS_FP8 family, get_grads_for_norm must follow the param.grad branch (not param.decoupled_grad).
trigger_conditions: FP8 training with non-delayed scaling (or DeepSeek-style FP8) so the no_fp8_or_ds_fp8 derived flag is False

bugs.title: z-loss metric tracking missing avg_group — not averaged across ranks
config.softmax_scale ignored in attention forward paths
aux_loss metric incorrectly scaled by TP world_size, missing reduce_group
bugs.category_origin: manual: matches M-NEW-30 judgment; aux_loss compute scaling bug

bugs.title: Attention norm modifies the residual stream
bugs.description: Attention norm 在应用于 attention block 之前意外修改了残差流，导致初始 loss 从 10 暴增到 60（v0.3.0 → v0.4.0），是严重的训练退化
bugs.root_cause: x = self.attn_norm(x) overwrites the residual variable. Residual connection uses normed input instead of original input.
bugs.invariant: After attn_norm, the residual tensor must be the original input, not the normed version
bugs.detection_signal: 初始 loss 异常升高（从 ~10 到 ~60）；residual stream 在 attention norm 前后发生了不应有的变化

bugs.title: Z-loss calculation averaged over instances instead of tokens
bugs.description: Z-loss 计算错误地按 instance 平均而非按 token 平均，导致 Z-loss 对模型的正则化效果不正确
bugs.root_cause: z_loss / num_micro_batches instead of z_loss / batch_size_in_tokens (64x difference for seq_len=64)
bugs.invariant: z_loss denominator must be batch_size_in_tokens, not num_micro_batches
bugs.detection_signal: Z-loss 值的量级与预期不符；不同 sequence length 的 batch 产生不一致的正则化强度

expected_output.buggy: BUG DETECTED: z_loss uses num_micro_batches denominator

bugs.title: preserve_rng_state incorrectly set to False with dropout
bugs.description: Gradient checkpointing 时 preserve_rng_state 错误设为 False，导致 backward 的 recomputation 中 dropout mask 与 forward 不一致，产生错误梯度
bugs.root_cause: Boolean condition inverted: preserve_rng_state = (all_dropout==0) instead of not(all_dropout==0)
bugs.invariant: When dropout > 0, preserve_rng_state must be True
bugs.detection_signal: 使用 gradient checkpointing + dropout 时，forward 和 backward recomputation 产生不同的 activation 值

expected_output.buggy: BUG DETECTED: preserve_rng_state=False with dropout > 0

bugs.title: start_index not reset in data loader
bugs.description: 从 checkpoint 恢复训练时，data loader 的 start_index 在进入新 epoch 时未被重置为 0，导致新 epoch 从旧的 start_index 开始读数据，部分数据被跳过
bugs.root_cause: global_step not reset to 0 when restore_dataloader=False
bugs.invariant: When restore_dataloader=False, global_step must be reset to 0
bugs.detection_signal: multi-epoch 训练中，新 epoch 的 data ordering 与预期不符；部分训练数据在新 epoch 中被跳过

bugs.title: Wrong size calculation for QK layer norm with GQA
bugs.description: QK LayerNorm 的 size 计算错误，影响 attention 中 query/key 的归一化，可能导致注意力权重计算不准确
bugs.invariant: k_norm size must equal head_dim * n_kv_heads, not d_model // n_kv_heads
bugs.detection_signal: QK norm 后的 tensor shape 或归一化统计量与预期不符

bugs.title: SkipStepAdamW step state never incremented
bugs.description: SkipStepAdamW 的 state['step'] 从未被递增，导致 Adam 的 bias correction 始终使用 step=0，有效学习率是设定值的 2.2 倍，且无法正确衰减
bugs.root_cause: optimizer step counter stays at 0, biasing Adam bias correction
bugs.invariant: After N optimizer.step() calls, state['step'] must equal N
bugs.detection_signal: optimizer state 中 step 始终为 0；实际学习率是配置值的 ~2.2 倍；Adam 的 bias correction 未生效

bugs.title: Non-zero ranks reporting partially-reduced metrics
bugs.description: 分布式训练中非 rank-0 进程报告的 training metrics 是部分 reduce 的值（未做 all-reduce），导致各 rank 看到不同的 metric 值
bugs.root_cause: Throughput metrics not using reduce_type=max → partially-reduced values on non-zero ranks
bugs.invariant: Throughput metrics must use reduce_type=ReduceType.max
bugs.detection_signal: 不同 rank 上报告的 training loss/metric 值不一致（应该相同）

bugs.title: Initial LR not set in optimizer param_groups
bugs.description: 从 checkpoint 加载后，optimizer 的初始学习率没有被重置为配置值，导致 warmup 从错误的 LR 起点开始
bugs.root_cause: Missing initial_lr in param_groups breaks LR scheduler after checkpoint resume
bugs.invariant: After optimizer construction, all param_groups must contain initial_lr
bugs.detection_signal: checkpoint 恢复后 learning rate 与预期 schedule 不匹配；warmup 曲线不正确

bugs.title: Mixture rounding error causing sample repetition
bugs.description: SourceMixtureDataset 中 mixture 比例的 rounding error 导致训练末尾出现重复采样
bugs.root_cause: Missing global_batch_size in SourceMixtureDatasetConfig causes rounding error
bugs.invariant: Config must include global_batch_size for proper allocation
bugs.detection_signal: 训练末尾出现重复的 data sample；mixture 比例与配置值有微小偏差

bugs.title: SourceMixtureDatasetConfig overrides global random seed
bugs.description: 构建 SourceMixtureDatasetConfig 时意外覆盖了 Python random 模块的全局 RNG seed，影响后续所有使用 random 的操作的确定性
bugs.root_cause: build() calls random.seed(self.seed), corrupting global RNG state
bugs.invariant: build() must not call global random.seed()
bugs.detection_signal: 构建 dataset config 后 random.random() 的输出序列改变；训练不可复现

bugs.title: Incorrect label_mask tensor creation in NumpyPaddedFSLDataset
bugs.description: NumpyPaddedFSLDataset 中 label_mask tensor 创建逻辑错误，导致 padding token 的 mask 不正确，影响 loss 计算
bugs.root_cause: torch.ones_like(input_ids) creates int64 mask, padded with pad_token_id instead of bool+False
bugs.invariant: label_mask must be bool dtype with False padding
bugs.detection_signal: label_mask 对 padding 位置的标记不正确；loss 中包含了 padding token 的贡献

expected_output.buggy: BUG DETECTED: label_mask uses int64 dtype
expected_output.fixed: CLEAN: label_mask uses bool dtype with False padding

bugs.title: Integer overflow when tracking global flops
bugs.description: 全局 FLOPS 计算在大规模训练时发生整数溢出，导致 MFU 计算结果错误
bugs.root_cause: global_train_flops: int overflows after ~107K steps for 7B models
bugs.invariant: global flops tracking must use float to avoid overflow
bugs.detection_signal: MFU 值异常（超过 100% 或为负数）；FLOPS 统计值不合理

bugs.title: A100 peak flops specification 2x too low
bugs.description: A100 的 peak FLOPS 规格值被设置为实际值的一半，导致 MFU（Model FLOPS Utilization）计算结果被夸大为实际值的两倍
bugs.root_cause: A100 BF16 peak = 624 TFLOPS but code used 312 TFLOPS, inflating MFU to unrealistic values.
bugs.invariant: A100 BF16 peak flops must be 624 TFLOPS, not 312
bugs.detection_signal: A100 上报告的 MFU 异常高（可能 > 60-70%）；与其他框架报告的 MFU 不一致

expected_output.buggy: BUG DETECTED: 312 TFLOPS

bugs.title: RMSNorm uses L2 norm instead of root-mean-square — wrong normalization
bugs.root_cause: x.norm(2) is L2 norm (sqrt(sum(x^2))), not RMS (sqrt(mean(x^2)))
bugs.invariant: After RMSNorm, output.pow(2).mean(-1) should be approximately 1.0

bugs.title: grad_norm_exp_avg EMA self-referential update — adaptive clipping broken
SDP attention bias not cast to autocast dtype, -inf downcasts to NaNs in mixed precision
bugs.root_cause: The attention bias was created in fp32 with -inf masked positions and only cast to the input dtype at the SDP call. Under autocast, the SDP kernel runs in lower precision; downcasting -inf to bf16/fp16 yields valid -inf values that propagate through softmax and produce NaNs once tokens are masked. The fix uses torch.finfo(target_dtype).min and casts the bias before the SDP call.
bugs.invariant: attention output must not contain NaNs after softmax when an attention mask is provided

bugs.title: FLOPs counter multiplies per-sequence flops by global batch size every step instead of accumulating per token
bugs.root_cause: num_fwd_flops/num_bck_flops were computed per sequence (multiplied by max_sequence_length) and SpeedMonitor accumulated them with global_batch_size every step using +=. After resume, the running total was overwritten/reset per step rather than treated as cumulative tokens, so reported Gflops did not accumulate across resumes. Fix changes flops to per-token and assigns Gflops = (fwd+bck) * global_total_tokens / 1e9.
bugs.invariant: total_training_Gflops must be a strictly non-decreasing function of global_total_tokens across training resumes

bugs.title: clip_grads_and_collect_metrics reduces grad norm over the global PG instead of the HSDP shard PG
bugs.root_cause: When training with HSDP each replica holds a full copy of the gradients, so reducing per-shard gradient norms over the WORLD process group double-counts grads across replicas. The original code called dist.reduce/dist.all_reduce without specifying a process group, so they used WORLD instead of the shard group. The fix accepts an optional process_group argument and routes every reduce/all_reduce call through it.
bugs.invariant: after reducing gradient norm metrics, the per-replica total_grad_norm should equal the un-replicated full-model norm; with N replicas, using the WORLD group would multiply the value by N
trigger_conditions: gradient clipping or grad-norm metric collection enabled

bugs.title: Outlier-loss skip-step logic inverted: optimizer steps only when loss IS an outlier
bugs.root_cause: should_step was being AND-ed with is_outlier, meaning the optimizer only stepped on outlier steps and silently skipped normal training steps. The fix negates is_outlier so the optimizer steps on normal batches and skips outliers as intended.
bugs.invariant: optim.step() must be invoked on the vast majority of training steps; should_step should equal True on non-outlier batches
trigger_conditions: any training step where the detector reports is_outlier=False (the common case)

bugs.title: torch.device('mps') used as boolean check is always truthy, forces every run into MPS/CPU mode
bugs.root_cause: The condition `if torch.device('mps')` is always True because torch.device(...) returns a non-None Device object. As a result the script unconditionally rewrites init_device to 'mps' and disables distributed training even on CUDA hosts. Fix replaces the call with torch.backends.mps.is_available() and a corresponding CPU check.
bugs.invariant: after script bootstrap, cfg.distributed_strategy and cfg.model.init_device must reflect the actual available backend (CUDA when torch.cuda.is_available())

bugs.title: muP set_base_shapes rescales parameters again when loading from a checkpoint, doubling the muP scaling
bugs.root_cause: OLMo.__init__ unconditionally invoked set_base_shapes(self, mup_base_shapes) which applies muP rescaling to the parameters. When loading a checkpoint, parameters are already in muP-scaled space, so the rescale fires a second time and silently shrinks/grows weights by the muP factor. Fix adds a mup_rescale_params=False kwarg and passes it from from_checkpoint.
bugs.invariant: for muP runs, parameter norms after OLMo.from_checkpoint() must equal the parameter norms saved in the checkpoint
trigger_conditions: OLMo.from_checkpoint() (sharded or unsharded) called to resume training

bugs.title: Restart LR/weight-decay reset uses cfg.learning_rate for every param group, ignoring per-group muP scaling
bugs.root_cause: On restart Trainer.restore_checkpoint reset every group's lr/initial_lr/weight_decay to cfg.optimizer.learning_rate / cfg.optimizer.weight_decay. With muP, matrix-like groups have lr divided by width_mult, so this reset wiped out muP scaling and used the base LR for every group. The fix tags each muP group with mup_lr/mup_weight_decay and uses those when resetting.
bugs.invariant: after restart, group['lr'] for a muP matrix-like group equals cfg.lr / width_mult, not cfg.lr
trigger_conditions: param groups have different muP width multipliers

bugs.title: OLMoBlock 'normal' init divides ff_out by sqrt(2*n_layers), shrinking it 1/sqrt(2L) below the configured init_std
bugs.root_cause: In the 'normal' init branch ff_out.weight was further divided by sqrt(2 * n_layers) after init_normal, supposedly to compensate for it being a residual layer. This left the per-row std much smaller than the configured init_std and broke equivalence with the full_megatron path. Fix removes the post-init divisor and unifies the std/cutoff_factor selection across init_fn variants.
bugs.invariant: for init_fn=normal the std of OLMoBlock.ff_out.weight at initialization should equal config.init_std (within sampling noise), not config.init_std / sqrt(2*n_layers)
trigger_conditions: model has more than one layer

bugs.title: Attention causal mask inverted — future tokens attend to past
bugs.root_cause: 1 - triu() masks the lower triangle instead of upper, inverting causal attention
bugs.invariant: In causal attention, position 0 should only attend to itself (avg attended index = 0)

bugs.title: ff_out readout reset overwrites muP zero-init weights with normal-distribution values
bugs.root_cause: OLMo.reset_parameters always called init_normal on transformer.ff_out, including under muP where ff_out is a MuReadout that must be initialized to zero. The non-zero initialization breaks the muP coordinate-check property and changes the model's effective output scale at initialization. Fix skips init_normal on ff_out when use_mup is True.
bugs.invariant: for use_mup=true, transformer.ff_out.weight must be all zeros immediately after model construction

bugs.title: OLMoSequentialBlock.ff_proj is silently zero-initialized via MuReadout when use_mup is enabled
bugs.root_cause: When use_mup was true, ff_proj was constructed as MuReadout with readout_zero_init=True and reset_parameters skipped re-initializing it. Only the final output ff_out should be a MuReadout in muP; every block's ff_proj being zero-initialized wipes out the FFN contribution at start of training. Fix only uses MuReadout for ff_proj when mlp_hidden_size is also set and always re-initializes ff_proj via init_normal.
bugs.invariant: for use_mup=true (and default mlp_hidden_size), each block's ff_proj.weight must have non-zero std after initialization

bugs.title: muP attention scale uses 1/d instead of sqrt(base_d)/d, mismatching the SP scale at the base width
bugs.root_cause: Under muP the attention scale was 1/q.size(-1), which differs from the standard parameterization scale 1/sqrt(d) even at the base width. This silently changes the attention temperature for the base model relative to SP. Fix uses sqrt(mup_base_n_heads)/q.size(-1) so that the scale matches SP exactly when n_heads == mup_base_n_heads and tracks muP scaling rules for wider models.
bugs.invariant: when use_mup=true and n_heads==mup_base_n_heads, attn_scale must equal 1/sqrt(head_dim) (the SP scale)

bugs.title: norm_after path applies attn_norm to (att_proj output) instead of to the attention output, leaving residual unnormed
bugs.root_cause: Under norm_after, attn_norm was being applied to the QKV projection output (qkv = attn_norm(att_proj(x))) before splitting and computing attention. The Post-LN attention design requires applying attn_norm to the attention output before the residual add. This silently changes the model semantics from Post-LN attention to a normalized-QKV attention.
bugs.invariant: for norm_after=true, the tensor flowing into att_proj must be unnormed; attn_norm must be applied to the attention output (att) prior to the residual add

bugs.title: global_step not reset when restore_dataloader=False, so resumed runs keep the checkpoint's step counter
bugs.root_cause: When the user sets restore_dataloader=False to start from saved weights but a fresh dataset, restore_checkpoint() resets epoch and token counters but forgot to reset global_step. The optimizer/LR scheduler then starts at the checkpoint's step (e.g., 50000) instead of 0, silently skipping warmup and using a much smaller LR than expected.
bugs.invariant: when cfg.restore_dataloader is False after restore_checkpoint(), self.global_step must equal 0
trigger_conditions: training resumes from a checkpoint with cfg.restore_dataloader=False
training is supposed to start a new run from the saved weights

bugs.title: Multi-epoch training does not reset dataset.start_index, so the next epoch resumes from the previous epoch's offset
bugs.root_cause: On epoch rollover Trainer reset epoch counters and called dataset.reshuffle(), but never reset dataset.start_index. The IterableDataset therefore skipped the first global_train_examples_seen_this_epoch instances of the new epoch, silently dropping them from training.
bugs.invariant: at the start of every epoch, self.dataset.start_index must equal 0
trigger_conditions: training spans more than one epoch (max_epochs > 1)

bugs.title: Restart in later epochs uses seed+epoch as PRNG seed, mixing epoch into seed irreversibly and corrupting reshuffle
bugs.root_cause: IterableDataset was constructed with seed=seed+(train_config.epoch or 0) and reshuffle() did self.seed += 1. After a restart at epoch=N the dataset received seed+N as base and then was incremented again, producing a different shuffle order than the original run had used at the same epoch. This silently changed the data ordering across resumes.
bugs.invariant: the global indices produced by IterableDataset for (seed, epoch) must be identical across a fresh run and a resumed run
trigger_conditions: training resumes from a checkpoint that is past the first epoch

bugs.title: Optimizer metric tensors are kept on CPU, causing per-rank cross-device mismatch on the all_reduce path
bugs.root_cause: per_param_min/max/sum/norm tensors were appended without explicit device, defaulting to CPU. The subsequent dist.all_reduce was then performed on CPU tensors while NCCL only supports GPU tensors; this either silently used the gloo backend (different reduction semantics, slower) or returned partially-reduced values when ranks ended up on different devices. Fix forces all metric tensors to the GPU device.
bugs.invariant: every tensor passed to dist.all_reduce/dist.reduce in clip_grads_and_collect_metrics must reside on the CUDA device, not CPU

bugs.title: z_loss mean reduction divides by mask fraction instead of masked mean
bugs.root_cause: z_squared / mask.mean() instead of (z_squared * mask).mean() — wrong reduction
bugs.invariant: z_loss with mean reduction should be a scalar; buggy version returns unreduced tensor

bugs.title: MoE load-balance and z-loss aux losses logged without all-reduce, so each rank reports its local value
bugs.root_cause: In Trainer the cross-entropy and z-loss were reduced across all ranks before logging, but lb_batch_loss (MoE load-balancing loss) and moe_z_batch_loss were missed. Each rank logged its local value, so the wandb metric reflected only rank 0's mini-batch instead of the global mean, giving misleading load-balance behavior and misreporting MoE training health.
bugs.invariant: after the metric reduction block, lb_batch_loss and moe_z_batch_loss must be identical on every rank (mean across ranks)

bugs.title: Optimizer collects metrics with num_model_replicas == 1 hardcoded, so HSDP norms are N times too large
bugs.root_cause: Optimizer.clip_grads_and_collect_metrics divided by a hardcoded num_model_replicas=1 even when HSDP was using multiple replicas. Each replica contributed identical gradient norms; without dividing by the replica count, all_reduce sums them and the reported norm is N times the true value, leading to spurious clipping decisions and wrong logged grad_norm.
bugs.invariant: with N model replicas in HSDP, all_reduced grad_norm metric must be divided by N before being reported

bugs.title: Reduced sums/norms not divided by num_model_replicas in HSDP, optimizer metrics inflated by replica count
bugs.root_cause: After the dist.all_reduce(SUM) in HYBRID_SHARD, identical replica contributions are summed N times. The original code consumed those sums directly, so per-param avg metrics and grad_norm metrics ended up N times larger than the true value. Fix divides the all-reduced tensor (all_sums_norms_numels and all_norms) by self.num_model_replicas before splitting and using.
bugs.invariant: for HSDP with N replicas, sum_after_all_reduce / N must equal the true global sum; per_param_avg_metrics computed from this should match a reference single-replica run

bugs.title: FullCheckpointer rebuilds optim state with old parameter keys, dropping state for renamed params after block_group_size change
bugs.root_cause: _make_state_dict_compatible returned a remapped state_dict but FullCheckpointer threw away the og_keys_to_new mapping when calling load_fsdp_optim_state. The optimizer state was then loaded against the new model keys without translation, so optimizer state for many params was either silently zeroed or attached to the wrong tensor.
bugs.invariant: after FullCheckpointer.restore_checkpoint with load_optimizer_state=True, optimizer.state must contain entries for every parameter in fsdp_model.parameters() and the values must match the saved checkpoint
trigger_conditions: training resumes with a different block_group_size than at save time

bugs.title: param-group classifier uses '.norm.' regex requiring trailing dot, treating q_norm/k_norm/ff_norm leaf weights as decay params
bugs.root_cause: get_param_groups identified norm parameters via the substring '.norm.' which only matches when there is a child name after .norm. For QK layer norms (q_norm.weight, k_norm.weight) the FQN ends with '.q_norm.weight' so the dot after norm never appears and the weight is silently routed to the decay group, applying weight_decay to a normalization layer's gain.
bugs.invariant: all parameters whose name contains '.norm' (with or without a child) must end up in the no_decay group when no_decay_norm_and_bias is true
trigger_conditions: model has LayerNorm/RMSNorm modules whose param fully-qualified name does not have anything after .norm (e.g. blocks.0.attn.q_norm.weight)

bugs.title: all_sums_norms_numels concatenated along last dim and reduced wrongly, mixing sums/norms/numels into one slot
bugs.root_cause: all_sums.unsqueeze(-1), all_norms.unsqueeze(-1), all_numels.unsqueeze(-1) were concatenated on dim=-1 and then reduced. After dist.reduce, all_sums_norms_numels.split(1) split per-parameter rows instead of separating the three categories, so the per-param avg metrics became a meaningless mix of sums/norms/numels.
bugs.invariant: after dist.reduce and split(1), the three pieces all_sums/all_norms/all_numels must each have shape (num_params,)
trigger_conditions: collect_param_metrics path that combines sums, norms, and numels into one all-reduce

bugs.title: DataConfig defaults memmap_dtype to uint16 silently, so vocab_size > 2^16 truncates token ids on load
bugs.root_cause: Before this commit MemMapDataset was constructed without passing a memmap_dtype, defaulting to uint16. When the actual on-disk file was uint32 (because vocab_size > 2^16), reading two-byte chunks silently produced wrong token ids without any type error. Fix exposes effective_memmap_dtype on DataConfig and threads it through build_memmap_dataset.
bugs.invariant: MemMapDataset(memmap_dtype) must equal np.uint32 (or wider) when train_config.model.vocab_size > 2**16
trigger_conditions: MemMap dataset built from train_config without an explicit dtype

bugs.title: _do_adaptive_clipping/_do_global_fixed_clipping hardcode collect_param_metrics=True, forcing per-step host-device sync and ignoring metrics_log_interval
bugs.root_cause: The clipping helpers were called with collect_param_metrics=True every step, regardless of the outer collect_param_metrics flag. This silently bypassed the metrics_log_interval gate (forcing host-device sync to compute clipping_rate every step) and produced metric values that did not match the requested logging cadence.
bugs.invariant: when collect_param_metrics is False at the outer call, _do_adaptive_clipping/_do_global_fixed_clipping must also be invoked with collect_param_metrics=False and clipping_rate must not be added to all_metrics

bugs.title: RoPE sin/cos missing type_as — dtype mismatch in mixed precision
bugs.root_cause: pos_sin/pos_cos cached in float32, not cast to match q_ dtype (bf16/fp16)
bugs.invariant: In apply_rotary_pos_emb, pos_sin.dtype and pos_cos.dtype must match t.dtype

bugs.title: Mitchell init hardcodes cutoff_factor=3.0, ignoring user-supplied init_cutoff_factor across blocks and embeddings
bugs.root_cause: Every Mitchell-init code path (OLMoBlock, OLMoSequentialBlock, OLMoLlamaBlock, and OLMo wte init) literally assigned cutoff_factor = 3.0, completely ignoring config.init_cutoff_factor. User configs that set a different cutoff (e.g. 4 or 6) silently produced narrower truncated-normal weight distributions than requested.
bugs.invariant: for init_fn=mitchell, the cutoff_factor used by init_normal must equal config.init_cutoff_factor (falling back to 3.0 only when None)

bugs.title: Final linear-decay scheduler uses wrong start/end factors (decays from 1.0 to alpha_f instead of alpha_f to alpha_f^2)
bugs.root_cause: The final linear decay segment is meant to take over after a cosine schedule has already decayed the LR to alpha_f * base_lr. The buggy version constructed `LinearLR(start_factor=1.0, end_factor=alpha_f)` which jumps the LR back up to the base learning rate at the handoff, and then decays only to alpha_f over the tail. The correct settings continue from `alpha_f` down to `alpha_f**2`. Result is a silent LR spike + wrong final LR.
bugs.invariant: scheduler.get_last_lr() must be continuous across the cosine-to-linear handoff at step=t_max
trigger_conditions: scheduler concatenates cosine-with-warmup followed by linear final decay
Training enters the post-cosine linear segment (global_step > t_max)

bugs.title: Embedding init std missing sqrt(d_model) factor — embeddings 16x too small
bugs.root_cause: init_std used directly instead of init_std * sqrt(d_model) for embeddings
bugs.invariant: embedding weight std should be init_std * sqrt(d_model)

bugs.title: IterableDataset leftover indices distributed wrongly across workers
bugs.root_cause: When distributing the leftover (unaligned) indices across workers, the buggy code did `left_overs = indices[truncated_size + worker_info.id : truncated_size + worker_info.id + worker_info.num_workers]`, which gives each worker a contiguous slice of `num_workers` indices starting at its id (so workers overlap and miss other leftovers). The fix uses strided slicing `indices[truncated_size + worker_info.id :: worker_info.num_workers]` so each worker independently picks its share.
bugs.invariant: Union of leftover indices across all workers must equal the full set of leftover indices, with no overlap
trigger_conditions: Total indices not divisible by device_batch_size

bugs.title: Dataset start_index not reset when starting a new epoch
bugs.root_cause: On epoch rollover the trainer set `self.epoch = epoch + 1` and reset `global_train_examples_seen_this_epoch = 0`, called `dataset.reshuffle()`, but forgot to reset `self.dataset.start_index = 0`. The IterableDataset therefore continued slicing the new (reshuffled) global indices starting from the previous epoch's offset, dropping that prefix of the new epoch and shortening it by the same amount.
bugs.invariant: At the start of every epoch the dataset must yield exactly len(dataset) examples in that epoch

bugs.title: Block readout init unconditionally re-initializes ff_proj, overwriting muP zero-init
bugs.root_cause: OLMoSequentialBlock.reset_parameters unconditionally called `init_normal(self.ff_proj, std, cutoff_factor, ...)`. When `use_mup=True`, ff_proj is a `MuReadout` module whose readout weights must remain at the muP zero/special initialization; the unconditional re-init overwrites that with a regular truncated-normal, silently breaking the muP coordinate-check guarantee that activation magnitudes are width-independent.
bugs.invariant: If use_mup=True, ff_proj.weight at end of init must remain at MuReadout's zero/scaled init (not truncated-normal with std=init_std)
trigger_conditions: use_mup enabled OR full_megatron init_fn (where ff_proj should keep MuReadout's zero init)

bugs.title: q_norm forced to elementwise_affine=True regardless of attention_layer_norm_with_affine
bugs.root_cause: When constructing QK normalization layers, `k_norm` correctly used `elementwise_affine=config.attention_layer_norm_with_affine` but `q_norm` was hard-coded to `elementwise_affine=True`. With `attention_layer_norm_with_affine=False` the model silently normalizes q with learnable scale/bias but k without, breaking symmetry between q and k and adding parameters that the user did not request.
bugs.invariant: q_norm.weight.requires_grad == k_norm.weight.requires_grad; both must follow attention_layer_norm_with_affine

bugs.title: Token embedding sized by vocab_size instead of embedding_size, mismatching ff_out width
bugs.root_cause: wte was constructed with `nn.Embedding(config.vocab_size, ...)` but the output projection `ff_out` was sized for `config.embedding_size or config.vocab_size`. When embedding_size > vocab_size, ff_out has more output classes than the embedding table has rows, so the extra logits backprop into nothing on the embedding side and the loss is computed over rows that have no corresponding learnable embedding. Logits for ids in [vocab_size, embedding_size) silently bias the softmax denominator.
bugs.invariant: wte.num_embeddings must equal ff_out.out_features (= embedding_size or vocab_size)
trigger_conditions: embedding_size set distinct from vocab_size (e.g. embedding_size=50304, vocab_size=50257—padded for hardware alignment)

bugs.title: Flash attention input layout wrong — head and sequence dims swapped
bugs.root_cause: flash_attn expects (B,S,H,D) but receives (B,H,S,D) without transpose
bugs.invariant: flash_attn input dim1 must be seq_len, not num_heads

bugs.title: Missing reset_parameters() after FSDP wrap on torch>=2.1 leaves model with default-initialized weights
bugs.root_cause: Starting in torch 2.1, FSDP no longer triggers the user's reset_parameters() automatically when materializing meta-device parameters. The buggy script created the OLMo model with init_device='meta', wrapped with FSDP, and never explicitly called `olmo_model.reset_parameters()` afterwards. Parameters are therefore left with whatever default contents FSDP produces (effectively uninitialized/zero-filled), silently destroying the carefully designed init scheme.
bugs.invariant: After FSDP wrap, summary stats of every parameter must match the init_fn's expected mean/std

bugs.title: ff_out nn.Linear constructed without device=init_device, breaking meta-init flow
bugs.root_cause: When building the readout `ff_out`, every other Linear in the model passed `device=config.init_device` so it could be created on the meta device and later materialized by FSDP with the configured init. The buggy version omitted this kwarg for `ff_out`, so it was always built on the default device with default kaiming init, escaping the init pipeline. The readout therefore carries the wrong init scale and lives on the wrong device until FSDP later moves it.
bugs.invariant: After model construction, every learnable parameter's device must equal config.init_device

bugs.title: load_model in mup coord-check skips reset_parameters when infshapes is None
bugs.root_cause: `reset_parameters()` was nested inside `if infshapes is not None:` together with `apply_infshapes`. For the standard-parametrization baseline (`infshapes=None`) the code therefore skipped reset_parameters entirely, leaving FSDP-materialized parameters with their default (often near-zero) values. Comparison curves and any downstream training look completely off without raising an error.
bugs.invariant: olmo_model.reset_parameters() must be called whenever the model is freshly built, regardless of mup mode
trigger_conditions: mup_olmo coord-check load_model path used for SP (standard-param) baseline
infshapes argument is None (i.e. running the SP comparison rather than a muP run)

bugs.title: DeepSpeed scheduler set to WarmupLR instead of WarmupDecayLR (no decay phase)
bugs.root_cause: DeepSpeedTrainer built its DeepSpeed config with `"scheduler": {"type": "WarmupLR", ...}`. WarmupLR only ramps up to the max LR and then holds it constant—it never decays. The intended schedule was WarmupDecayLR which ramps then linearly decays. Buggy training therefore runs at peak LR for the entire post-warmup duration, silently overshooting the planned schedule.
bugs.invariant: After warmup, learning rate must be monotonically decreasing toward warmup_min_lr; not constant
trigger_conditions: DeepSpeedTrainer in use (configs ending in -lumi-deepspeed.yaml etc.)
Long enough training that decay matters

bugs.title: DeepSpeed warmup_min_lr=0 instead of base_lr*0.1, also missing warmup_type=linear
bugs.root_cause: DeepSpeedTrainer hard-coded `warmup_min_lr=0.0` and omitted `warmup_type='linear'`. Combined, the warmup ramp starts from exactly 0 (rather than 10% of base lr) and uses DeepSpeed's default warmup interpolation, producing a different shape than the OLMo trainer for the equivalent config. Training runs to completion but with a silently mismatched warmup schedule.
bugs.invariant: DeepSpeed warmup LR profile must match the OLMo trainer's warmup profile for an equivalent configuration

bugs.title: Newest checkpoint deleted by retention policy because it is appended after pruning
bugs.root_cause: Both `save_checkpoint` and `save_unsharded_checkpoint` appended the freshly-saved directory to `self.checkpoints`/`self.unsharded_checkpoints` *after* the deletion loop. The deletion loop ran on the old list (without the new entry), then the new entry was appended—but on the *next* save the just-saved checkpoint was already at the end and could be evicted in the wrong order. The fix appends before the dist.barrier so retention always sees the new entry.
bugs.invariant: After save_checkpoint(N), the directory step{N} must remain on disk and self.checkpoints must reflect the actual contents of save_folder
trigger_conditions: List already contains save_num_checkpoints_to_keep entries when a new save fires

bugs.title: Train DataLoader max_steps not multiplied by device_train_batch_size
bugs.root_cause: `build_train_dataloader` passed `max_steps=train_config.max_duration` to the IterableDataset, but max_steps for the dataset is measured in *examples*, not optimizer steps. With device_train_batch_size > 1 the dataset truncates itself to max_duration examples instead of max_duration*batch_size examples, so the loader exhausts after roughly 1/batch_size of the planned training. Likewise `start_step` was not scaled, so resume-from-step doesn't seek to the right example.
bugs.invariant: Total examples yielded by train loader = max_duration * device_train_batch_size

bugs.title: Ladder 150M model uses max_sequence_length=1024 instead of 2048
bugs.root_cause: MODEL_CONFIG_150M in scripts/ladder.py hard-coded `max_sequence_length=1024`, half the standard ladder context length of 2048. The model is built with positional structures (rope cache, default attention bias buffers) sized for 1024 and the loader truncates training sequences to 1024 tokens, silently wasting the second half of every example and producing per-token loss numbers that are not comparable to the rest of the ladder.
bugs.invariant: Each tier in the ladder must use the same max_sequence_length (2048) so token-loss curves are comparable
trigger_conditions: scripts/ladder.py used to launch the 150M tier

bugs.title: Fused cross_entropy path passes lse_square_scale=0 so z-loss term is silently dropped
bugs.root_cause: In `fused_loss_fn` the call to FlashAttention's CrossEntropyLoss hard-coded `lse_square_scale=0.0`. That parameter is the multiplier for the auxiliary z-loss term that the fused kernel computes; setting it to 0 silently disables the z-loss in the fused path, even though the surrounding code believes z-loss is being applied (and adds it to the total loss with whatever value the kernel returned). With fused_loss enabled, training therefore runs without the intended z-regularization despite logging non-zero z_loss values.
bugs.invariant: z_loss returned by fused_loss_fn must have the same magnitude as z_loss returned by the python reference cross_entropy_loss for the same inputs

bugs.title: Ladder script uses eos_token_id=0 instead of dolma tokenizer's 50279
bugs.root_cause: `MODEL_CONFIG_150M` hard-coded `eos_token_id=0` even though the dolma GPT-NeoX tokenizer uses 50279 for end-of-document. With the wrong eos_token_id the model treats id 0 (an ordinary BPE token) as document boundary for chunk boundaries / loss masking, and never recognizes the real EOS appended by the tokenizer. Document boundary statistics and EOS-conditioned generation are silently wrong.
bugs.invariant: model.eos_token_id must equal tokenizer.eos_token_id (50279 for dolma GPT-NeoX)
trigger_conditions: scripts/ladder.py used to build the 150M model config

bugs.title: Wrong layer initialized — ff_out instead of ff_proj (variable name typo)
MoE load-balancing loss not divided by num_micro_batches in gradient accumulation loop
bugs.root_cause: Inside the per-micro-batch loop the buggy code added the full `batched_load_balancing_loss(self.moe_args)` to the per-micro-batch loss without dividing by `len(micro_batches)`. Because the auxiliary loss is computed per micro batch but enters the optimizer once per global batch via gradient accumulation, the LB regularizer is silently scaled by N (the number of micro batches), pushing the router much harder toward uniformity than configured.
bugs.invariant: Sum of LB-loss contributions over a global batch must equal `batched_load_balancing_loss` evaluated once on the global batch (independent of micro-batch count)

bugs.title: Attention norm overwrites residual input — destroys identity path
Token IDs silently truncated to 16-bit by modulo 2^16
soft_target_probs silently truncated from float to int by as_tensor()
bugs.root_cause: Local as_tensor() casts non-bool numpy arrays via astype(np.int_), destroying float probabilities
bugs.invariant: as_tensor(float_array) must preserve float dtype, not truncate to int

bugs.title: Qwen3 transformer config defaults rope_full_precision=True, diverging from HF that applies RoPE in bf16
bugs.root_cause: TransformerConfig.qwen3_* factories did not pass rope_full_precision=False, so olmo-core promoted q/k to fp32 around the rotary multiply while HuggingFace Qwen3 applies RoPE entirely in bf16. The fp32 round-off difference made post-RoPE q/k bit-non-identical and silently shifted training dynamics from the HF reference.
bugs.invariant: When matching HF Qwen3, the dtype of the tensor entering the rotary multiplication must equal the input attention dtype (bf16), not fp32.
trigger_conditions: Comparison or weight transfer with HuggingFace Qwen3 reference

bugs.title: Attention claude-init uses d_model**-0.5 instead of actual w.in_features**-0.5 — wrong std for GQA Q/K/V and w_out
bugs.root_cause: InitMethod.attention used a single std = d_model**-0.5 for Q/K/V and w_out. Under GQA the K/V projection input is still d_model but the constant assumed identical fan-in across all weights, and for w_out the actual fan-in is n_heads*head_dim which can differ from d_model. Initialization was therefore silently scaled wrong on these layers.
bugs.invariant: Init std for each linear layer w must equal w.in_features**-0.5 (true fan-in), not a single d_model-derived constant shared across all attention projections.
trigger_conditions: Attention has separated w_q/w_k/w_v with GQA (n_kv_heads != n_heads) so projections have different output dims
FusedAttention or w_out where in_features differs from d_model

bugs.title: Per-document RoPE positions not propagated when cu_doc_lens is provided in packed mode
bugs.root_cause: Attention.forward called self.rope(...) without forwarding the cu_doc_lens argument, so the second document in a packed sequence got global positions [k_doc1_len, ...] instead of restarting at 0. Documents that should have produced identical outputs silently received different rotary phases.
bugs.invariant: For two identical documents packed back-to-back, the post-RoPE q/k for both segments must match (intra-doc positions reset at each cu_doc_lens boundary).
trigger_conditions: Multiple documents packed into one sequence (intra-document masking)
cu_doc_lens is provided to attention forward

bugs.title: RotaryEmbedding cu_doc_lens path miscomputes positions for B>1 — second batch element reuses batch-0 doc layout
bugs.root_cause: The cu_doc_lens code path built positions = arange(k_len) without adding any per-batch offset, then ran searchsorted against the flat cumulative-doc-lens list. For B>1 the second batch element's positions were searched against batch-0 boundaries, producing wrong doc indices and wrong intra-doc positions whenever batch elements had different doc layouts.
bugs.invariant: Local positions computed for each (batch, token) must equal token_index minus the start of that token's document; batch elements with identical doc structure must give identical local_positions.
trigger_conditions: Batch size > 1 with different document boundaries per batch element

bugs.title: GatedDeltaNet A_log/dt_bias initialized as empty (uninit memory) and miss the GDN-prescribed init
bugs.root_cause: GatedDeltaNet's A_log was initialized via torch.log(uniform(0,16)) and dt_bias via inverse-softplus on uniform(dt_min, dt_max), but the surrounding generic InitMethod did not delegate to the mixer, so for hybrid models these parameters silently fell back to torch.empty (uninitialized memory) or default linear inits — producing wildly off-distribution updates with no error.
bugs.invariant: After init, GDN A_log lies in log(uniform(0,16)) and dt_bias is the inverse-softplus of dt sampled in [dt_min, dt_max]; their distribution must be checkable against this prescription.
trigger_conditions: Hybrid model includes GatedDeltaNet sequence mixer
Block init relied on the generic InitMethod path

bugs.title: MoE load-balancing aux loss accumulated to metrics twice when activation checkpointing recomputes the block
bugs.root_cause: compute_aux_loss accumulated the load-balancing scalar into the per-step metric on every forward call. Activation checkpointing reruns forward during backward, so the aux loss was added twice, producing wandb metrics that are 2x the true value (gradient is unaffected but anyone using the metric to tune the multiplier is misled).
bugs.invariant: Metric accumulation inside the MoE router must occur exactly once per global forward — recompute calls must skip the metrics side-effect.
trigger_conditions: Activation checkpointing enabled around the MoE block

bugs.title: Idealized-overlap ladder reads dolma2 (uint32) tokens with default uint16 dtype — silently produces garbage token ids
bugs.root_cause: PerFileChunkedInstanceSourceConfig defaulted token_dtype to uint16. dolma2 stores token IDs as uint32 because the vocab exceeds 65535. Reading the file as uint16 reinterprets each pair of bytes as a different token, so the model trained on totally fabricated token streams without any error.
bugs.invariant: Configured token_dtype must accommodate tokenizer.vocab_size (uint16 only when vocab <= 65535).

bugs.title: OLMo midtraining mix key references the wrong file — '0625' name maps to '0725' path
bugs.root_cause: The DataMix enum had OLMo_midtraining_mix_0625_100B = 'OLMo-midtraining-mix-0725-100B'. The mismatched value silently routed users to the July (0725) mix when they thought they were using the June (0625) mix, training on the wrong corpus.
bugs.invariant: DataMix enum string value must match its enum member name (date components agree).

bugs.title: QwenRMSNorm absent from olmo-core — RMSNorm casts back to og_dtype after weight multiply, diverging from HF Qwen3
bugs.root_cause: olmo-core's RMSNorm computed normalize -> weight-multiply -> cast(og_dtype), which performs the affine multiply in fp32. HF's Qwen3RMSNorm casts back to og_dtype before the weight multiply so the multiply happens in input bf16. Trained Qwen3 weights expect the bf16 ordering; computing the multiply in fp32 silently drifts on outlier-feature channels deep in the stack.
bugs.invariant: For Qwen3 layer norm the weight*x multiply executes in input dtype (bf16), not in fp32 — equivalently x is cast back to og_dtype before the affine.

bugs.title: Activation checkpointing skips RNG state preservation even when dropout is active — backward recomputes a different mask
bugs.root_cause: Transformer.apply_activation_checkpointing hard-coded preserve_rng_state=False with a TODO. With dropout active, the recomputed forward in backward used a fresh random mask, so backward gradients corresponded to a different forward graph than the one used to produce the loss — silently wrong gradients and degraded convergence.
bugs.invariant: If any nn.Dropout module exists, the forward run during backward recompute must use the same RNG state as the original forward (preserve_rng_state=True).
trigger_conditions: nn.Dropout module present in the model graph (dropout > 0)

bugs.title: Adam step counter not incremented — bias correction permanently wrong
bugs.root_cause: step.add_(step_factor) was commented out in adamw_step
bugs.invariant: optimizer state step must increment each training step

bugs.title: Expert/router gradients zeroed unconditionally in train_batch — first-half mask applied even when freeze_experts is off
bugs.root_cause: The base TransformerTrainModule.train_batch unconditionally walked named_parameters and zeroed the first half of expert and router gradients. The freeze logic was supposed to only run for the FreezeTransformerTrainModule subclass, but its train_batch override had been moved to module level, so the parent ran the masking on every regular training run silently — half of every expert never got updated.
bugs.invariant: When freeze_experts is unset/'none', no expert or router parameter gradient may be force-zeroed by the train module.
trigger_conditions: TransformerTrainModule (parent class) used directly without FreezeTransformerTrainModule
Model contains parameters whose names contain 'experts' or 'router'

bugs.title: Config encoding ignores field.init=False — non-init dataclass fields silently round-trip with stale values
bugs.root_cause: Config.as_dict iterated dataclasses.fields without filtering out fields whose init=False, so derived fields were dumped to the encoded dict and re-passed to the dataclass constructor on decode. Decode then either crashed on unknown kwargs or silently overwrote the post_init-derived value with a stale snapshot, breaking config round-trip equivalence.
bugs.invariant: Encoded Config dict must contain only fields whose .init is True; decoding then re-encoding must be a fixed point.
trigger_conditions: Config dataclass uses @dataclass with field(init=False) for derived fields
Config is serialized via Config.as_dict and re-decoded

bugs.title: RoPE positions use global token index in packed mode — second document gets [k_doc1_len, ...] instead of [0, ...]
bugs.root_cause: RotaryEmbedding.forward computed positions = arange(k_len) and indexed pos_sin/pos_cos directly, ignoring document boundaries. Two identical documents at different positions inside the packed batch produced different post-RoPE q/k, breaking the intra-document independence assumption used by document-aware attention masking.
bugs.invariant: Two identical documents packed back-to-back must yield identical post-RoPE q/k values (per-document positions reset at each cu_doc_lens boundary).
trigger_conditions: Multiple documents packed into one sequence

bugs.title: PerFileChunkedInstanceSourceConfig defaults token_dtype to uint16 — silent token-id corruption for vocab > 65535
bugs.root_cause: PerFileChunkedInstanceSourceConfig.token_dtype defaulted to uint16. When the on-disk file is uint32 the loader silently reinterprets each pair of bytes as a separate token, producing wrong but in-range token IDs that never error.
bugs.invariant: token_dtype default must match the tokenizer's required width; if not specified, must be inferred from tokenizer.vocab_size or the constructor must error.

bugs.title: MoEFusedV2Optimizer reduces PP grad norm with _combine_norm (sum-of-norms) instead of _reduce_norm — over-counts gradient magnitude
bugs.root_cause: When reducing total_grad_norm across the PP group, the code called self._combine_norm (which adds rank-local norms instead of squaring/all-reducing/sqrt). This over-estimated the global gradient norm, which then drove gradient clipping to scale every step too aggressively without raising any error.
bugs.invariant: Global grad-norm reduction across PP must satisfy sqrt(sum(local_norm**2)), equivalent to the existing _reduce_norm helper, not naive summation of norm magnitudes.

bugs.title: SamplingInstanceSource cache write race — concurrent ladder runs overwrite each other's index files
bugs.root_cause: Local rank-0 always rewrote the indices file at startup. Concurrent jobs sharing the work directory raced via tmp_path.replace, leaving training reading partially-written or shuffled indices. Because the file name embeds the fingerprint, the contents are guaranteed identical, so silently using a stale half-written file (or rebuilding into the same name as another job) gave inconsistent ordering across runs.
bugs.invariant: If the deterministic-fingerprint indices file already exists, the rank must not rewrite it; cross-rank reads of the file must agree.
trigger_conditions: Multiple training jobs share the same work_dir
SamplingInstanceSource used; rank-0 builds the cached indices file

bugs.title: memmap_to_write tmp filename uses seeded random — concurrent writers collide on identical path under the same RNG seed
bugs.root_cause: memmap_to_write picked the temp filename via random.randint(0, 2**32) seeded by the global Python RNG. With identical seeds across ranks, each rank generated the same tmp_path; one rank's tmp_path.replace removed the file another rank was about to read, causing FileNotFoundError-style silent data shadowing or partial-content reads when a fallback masked the error.
bugs.invariant: Concurrent writers of the same file must use unique temp paths (entropy independent of the deterministic seed) and a missing tmp_path due to a concurrent rename must succeed if the destination exists.
trigger_conditions: Multiple ranks/processes preprocess the same path with the same global random seed

bugs.title: MultiGroupDistributedDataParallel falls back to default group when dist is unavailable but never wires per-bucket grad reduce
bugs.root_cause: MoE-style parameters were reduced one-by-one through the existing DDP path, missing the view-based bucket optimization that batches grads of the same dtype/process_group into a single all-reduce. Under EP+DP MoE this both inflated NCCL volume and silently skipped the comm_dtype downcast on extra-large params, occasionally producing zero gradients for partial buckets.
bugs.invariant: Under MoE DDP each parameter's gradient must participate in exactly one all-reduce per step, with comm_dtype matching the configured bucket dtype.
trigger_conditions: MoE-shaped parameters require per-bucket grad reduction with view-based storage

bugs.title: Mamba.forward casts inputs using cached self.dtype — wrong dtype after FSDP wraps the conv1d weight
bugs.root_cause: Mamba.forward used self.dtype (snapshot at construction time) to cast x. After FSDP wrapped the inner conv1d, the actual parameter dtype changed but self.dtype was stale, so x flowed into the kernel in the wrong precision. The MambaSSM kernel still ran but produced silently wrong values.
bugs.invariant: Activation dtype entering Mamba.inner must equal the live conv1d weight dtype (recomputed per forward), not a constructor-time snapshot.
trigger_conditions: Mamba sequence mixer wrapped in FSDP / FSDP2
Mixed-precision params (e.g., bf16 weights, fp32 cast targets)

bugs.title: DTPBoundaryPredictor calls F.silu with two arguments — silu treats w3(h) as inplace flag, drops gating
bugs.root_cause: The expression F.silu(self.w1(h), self.w3(h)) passed self.w3(h) as the inplace argument of F.silu (PyTorch interprets the second positional as a bool-coerced inplace flag). The intended SwiGLU gate (silu(w1(h)) * w3(h)) never executed, so the FFN computed silu(w1(h)) alone and the boundary predictor produced silently degraded outputs.
bugs.invariant: FFN must implement gated SwiGLU: out = w2(silu(w1(h)) * w3(h)); silu must be called with exactly one tensor argument.
trigger_conditions: BLT DTPBoundaryPredictor used for byte-level training

bugs.title: sqrt decay LR schedule uses wrong formula — decay curve inverted
bugs.root_cause: sqrt(progress) instead of 1-sqrt(1-progress) — wrong decay curve shape
bugs.invariant: sqrt decay should decay fast initially, slow at end

bugs.title: MoE sigmoid router gives F.sigmoid(logits) without epsilon — exact-zero scores propagate as NaN through downstream log
bugs.root_cause: scores = F.sigmoid(logits) could underflow to exactly 0.0 under low precision, and downstream load-balancing or aux-loss code took log/divide of the score, producing -inf/NaN that silently propagated into the final loss without any explicit error.
bugs.invariant: Router score for gating_function=sigmoid must be strictly positive (>= eps) so subsequent log/divide operations are finite.
trigger_conditions: Highly negative logits causing sigmoid output ~ 0 in bf16/fp16

bugs.title: fused_linear_cross_entropy_loss accumulates gradient in bf16 by default — silently noisier than fp32 accumulation
bugs.root_cause: The liger-kernel fused linear+CE call defaulted accum_grad to bf16, which silently degraded gradient precision on the LM head. The numerical noise was small enough that training continued, but it shifted loss curves vs the unfused baseline.
bugs.invariant: Backward gradient accumulation for the LM head fused kernel must be in fp32 even when forward inputs are bf16.

bugs.title: fan_in init for embeddings ignores embed_scale — embeddings remain std=1.0 and become huge after scaling
bugs.root_cause: init_embeddings under fan_in always used std=1.0. The transformer then multiplied embeddings by embed_scale (e.g., sqrt(d_model)) at the input, producing embeddings several orders of magnitude larger than intended. Training did not error but the input magnitude scrambled the early-layer dynamics.
bugs.invariant: After init_embeddings followed by the embed_scale multiply, the embedding output std must stay near 1.0 (compensating the fan-in init by 1/embed_scale).
trigger_conditions: Transformer config sets embed_scale (e.g., Gemma-like models)

bugs.title: NumpyDataLoaderBase double-counts tokens_processed — counter advances both inside and outside the iterator
bugs.root_cause: NumpyDataLoaderBase incremented self.tokens_processed += self.global_batch_size inside its __iter__ in addition to the trainer-level update, double-counting tokens. On resume the loader skipped twice as many batches as it should, silently advancing past unseen data.
bugs.invariant: tokens_processed must increase by exactly global_batch_size per yielded batch, not 2x.
trigger_conditions: Resume from checkpoint that used the same data loader

bugs.title: ComplexRotaryEmbedding ignores cu_doc_lens — packed-document positions never reset for complex-RoPE blocks
bugs.root_cause: ComplexRotaryEmbedding.forward did not accept cu_doc_lens, so even when callers tried to enable per-document positions for complex-RoPE blocks, the call site silently fell through to global positions and the rotary phase still depended on global token index across packed boundaries.
bugs.invariant: Per-document positions used by complex-RoPE must reset at each cu_doc_lens boundary; identical packed documents must yield identical post-RoPE q/k.
trigger_conditions: Model uses ComplexRotaryEmbedding (complex-number RoPE) instead of standard RotaryEmbedding

bugs.title: Evaluator iterates with stale data-loader state — second eval pass starts mid-stream, evaluating a different subset
bugs.root_cause: Evaluator.__iter__ called reshuffle() but did not reset() the data loader. tokens_processed/batches_processed from the previous (truncated) eval persisted, so the next eval pass started reading from the stale offset instead of batch 0. Repeated evals on the same checkpoint silently scored on different data subsets.
bugs.invariant: Two consecutive Evaluator passes over the same checkpoint must read the same first-N batches when deterministic=True (epoch pinned).
trigger_conditions: LM evaluator runs multiple passes with eval_duration truncating each pass
DataLoaderBase carried over batches_processed from the previous pass

bugs.title: Trainer async bookkeeping callback fires after future is FINISHED — state_dict snapshot can capture pre-callback state
bugs.root_cause: _run_bookkeeping_op attached cb via future.add_done_callback. add_done_callback runs after the future is marked FINISHED, so _join_bookkeeping_ops returned before cb ran, and a state_dict() capture immediately after could observe stale callback state (e.g., un-rotated checkpoint indexes).
bugs.invariant: All bookkeeping callbacks for a future must complete before that future transitions to FINISHED so _join_bookkeeping_ops waits on them too.
trigger_conditions: Trainer launches a bookkeeping op (e.g., async checkpoint save) that has a completion cb

bugs.title: Grad clipper recorded grad_norm DTensor — record_metric saw distributed value
bugs.root_cause: GradClipperCallback recorded the raw grad_norm output from torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ without unwrapping it. With TP, this returned a DTensor; the metric system then operated on the DTensor across ranks, producing a wrongly reduced grad-norm value while clipping itself was already applied locally.
bugs.invariant: Values passed to record_metric with reduce_type=None must be plain tensors representing per-call values, never DTensors with implicit replication semantics.

bugs.title: PP grad-norm clip used per-PP-stage local norm without all-reducing across PP ranks
bugs.root_cause: TransformerTrainModule.optim_step took grad_norm from the per-stage clip path without summing the squared norms across PP ranks first. Each PP stage sees only its local parameters, so the unreduced norm is a fraction of the global norm; clipping uses too small a divisor, leaving gradients larger than max_grad_norm.
